Need to search first.I couldn't write any notes on Isaiah 24 this time, because I wasn't able to read a single source page. My first attempt to open eight commentary pages at once hit the tool's usage limit. On a single retry, the tool refused the link because a site has to come up in a search before its page can be opened. Then the one search I ran was blocked because I had no tool calls left for this turn.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say and never fill gaps from my own knowledge. So I haven't written anything from memory, and there are no URLs to give.

If you ask again in a new turn, I'll work through the sources one at a time:
1. **Verse-by-verse reading:** Enduring Word, Bible Hub (Ellicott, Gill, Pulpit Commentary, Barnes), Wesley's notes on StudyLight, and Precept Austin.
2. **Where Protestant traditions differ:** Likely points are v. 5 (what "the everlasting covenant" is), vv. 1–13 (a judgment in Isaiah's day or a worldwide end-time one), and vv. 21–22 (who "the host of heaven" are, and what being "punished after many days" means). I'd look for each tradition's own teachers on these.
3. **Other views:** NET Bible notes and Bible Odyssey (including the common scholarly label "Isaiah Apocalypse" for chapters 24–27), plus Catholic and Orthodox sources such as New Advent's Church Fathers.

To stay within the limits, it may help to split the job into three requests: verses 1–6, 7–16, and 17–23.
